title: LU Decomposition and QR Factorization vs Cramer's Rule
description: Extends the Gaussian vs Cramer complexity comparison to LU decomposition and QR factorization. LU (n³ model) beats Cramer for all n ≥ 1; QR (2n³ model) beats Cramer for n ≥ 3. The gap grows super-polynomially: for any constant K, all O(n³) algorithms are eventually K-times more efficient than Cramer's O(n·n!).

originalContributions: LU complexity model: luMuls n = n³ (same O-class as Gaussian elimination)
QR complexity model: qrMuls n = 2n³ (conservative upper bound, same O-class)
lu_beats_cramer: LU (n³) < Cramer ((n+1)·n·n!) for all n ≥ 1
qr_beats_cramer_from_3: QR (2n³) < Cramer ((n+1)·n·n!) for n ≥ 3 (at n=1: tie; at n=2: QR worse)
Key lemma: 2n³ < n²·n! for n ≥ 4, proved via 2n³ < n⁴ = n²·n² < n²·n!
Asymptotic result: for any K, QR is eventually K-times more efficient than Cramer
Three-way comparison: Gaussian ≤ QR ≤ 2·Gaussian < Cramer (for n ≥ 4)
Formal confirmation: all cubic solvers belong to the same algorithmic class

proofStrategy: Extends CramersRuleOQ02.lean by defining LU and QR complexity models and proving each beats Cramer. The key new lemma (two_n_cube_lt_sq_factorial) shows 2n³ < n²·n! via the chain 2n³ < n⁴ = n²·n² < n²·n! (using factorial_gt_sq from the parent). The asymptotic result uses the threshold n ≥ max(4, 2K) to ensure K·2 ≤ n.

mainTheorems.name: luMuls_eq_gaussMuls
mainTheorems.description: LU decomposition has the same leading complexity as Gaussian elimination in our model: luMuls n = gaussMuls n = n³.

mainTheorems.name: qr_beats_cramer
mainTheorems.description: QR factorization (2n³ multiplications) is strictly faster than Cramer's rule ((n+1)·n·n!) for n ≥ 4, proved via the chain 2n³ < n²·n! ≤ (n+1)·n·n!.

mainTheorems.name: qr_asymptotically_better
mainTheorems.description: For any constant K, QR factorization is eventually K-times more efficient than Cramer's rule: ∃N, ∀n≥N, K·2n³ < (n+1)·n·n!.

mainTheorems.name: three_way_comparison
mainTheorems.description: For n ≥ 4: luMuls n = gaussMuls n ≤ qrMuls n < cramersRuleMuls n — all O(n³) algorithms outperform Cramer's O(n·n!).

mainTheorems.name: lu_qr_vs_cramer_summary
mainTheorems.description: Comprehensive summary: LU/QR models, both beat Cramer for n ≥ 4, and both beat Cramer asymptotically by any multiplicative constant.
